This article describes what `readboe` knows before it goes online and what a
retrieval adds to that record. The examples use the package's committed
snapshots and registries, so they are deterministic and do not require a live
Bank of England connection.

## Coverage and source map

| Source surface | Offline discovery | Network reader | Main identity to retain |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Bankstats-linked IADB series and revisions | `boe_catalogue()` | `read_boe_series()`, `boe_series_metadata()`, `boe_series_updates()` | IADB `series_id`, date range, format, update mode |
| Bankstats catalogue and bulk workbooks | `boe_catalogue()`, `boe_bankstats_assets()` | `read_boe_bankstats()`, `read_boe_bankstats_series()` | series ID plus table/member and workbook coordinates |
| Official Bank Rate and fixed rate identities | `boe_rate_series()` | `boe_bank_rate_history()`; registered identities through `read_boe_series()` | Bank Rate event period/precision or exact IADB `series_id` |
| Fitted yield curves | `boe_yield_assets()` | `read_boe_yield_curve()` | asset family, member, sheet, row, and column |
| Statistical and research release families | `boe_release_registry()` and, when present, `boe_release_assets()` | `read_boe_release_asset()` | release family and exact asset URL |

The offline calls do not infer a result from a current web page. They read
hash-authenticated package data and return the snapshot's exact rows.

The 3 August 2026 snapshot covers 5,252 IADB-validated identities across 60
current Bankstats tables. All carry series-specific canonical bounds; the
snapshot's overall history envelope is June 1969 to July 2026. It spans seven
subject sections: money and lending; monetary-financial-institution balance
sheets, income, and expenditure; deposits and lending; interest and exchange
rates; public-sector debt and money-market operations; capital issuance; and
financial derivatives. Frequencies comprise 4,355 monthly, 845 quarterly, 21
annual, 21 weekly, and 10 daily identities.

The current Bankstats ZIP has 64 workbook members: 5,008 catalogue identities
have an exact workbook cell, while 244 retain the canonical full-history route
only. The separate Bank Rate workbook begins in October 1694. The yield
registry covers 11 latest/archive file identities across five curve families,
and the release registry names 14 families; see the README's
[coverage table](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboe#coverage-at-a-glance) for
their historical boundaries and current release-asset limitation.

## Catalogue scope and receipts

The manifest is the first object to inspect when a reproducible workflow starts.
It states the snapshot scope, build time, row counts, source URLs, and hashes
of the catalogue and its receipts. The snapshot date is data, not the current
clock, and should be recorded alongside results.

```{r manifest}
library(readboe)

manifest <- boe_catalogue_manifest()
manifest[, c(
  "generated_at_utc", "catalogue_scope", "catalogue_complete_within_scope",
  "catalogue_rows", "metadata_rows", "canonical_history_series",
  "bankstats_workbook_members"
)]
```

The build receipts provide the source-page retrieval evidence used to create
the snapshot. They are not a replacement for a retrieval receipt from a later
live data request.

```{r receipts}
search_receipt <- boe_catalogue_receipts(kind = "search", limit = 1L)
search_receipt[, c(
  "surface", "catalogue_scope", "retrieved_at", "status", "raw_bytes",
  "raw_sha256", "link_rows", "retrievable_series"
)]
```

Network readers accept a caller-owned absolute deadline. Constructing one is
an offline operation, and the same object can be passed through a multi-step
retrieval workflow so retries cannot silently extend its time budget.

```{r deadline}
fixed_deadline <- boe_deadline(
  at = as.POSIXct("2030-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
c(class = class(fixed_deadline)[[1L]], deadline_utc = format(fixed_deadline, tz = "UTC"))
```

The package verifies the paired snapshot hash before returning the default
catalogue or manifest. A hash mismatch, corrupt file, or schema mismatch is a
typed `readboe_identity_mismatch`, `readboe_cache_corruption`, or
`readboe_schema_drift` condition rather than a silently changed result.

## Browse exact identities and facets

Queries and facets are useful for a user interface or a review step before a
network request. Here the query is deliberately small and the output is
limited, while the facet counts describe every row surviving the filter.

```{r browse}
candidate <- boe_catalogue(query = "capital issuance", limit = 3L)
candidate[, c("series_id", "displayed_code", "label", "frequency", "table_id")]

facets <- boe_catalogue_facets(query = "capital issuance")
facets[c("frequency", "section", "surface_membership")]
```

The `boe_catalogue_provenance` attribute on `candidate` includes the matched
row count before `limit` was applied. The row values remain official labels and
identifiers; `readboe` does not turn them into a guessed product or economic
interpretation.

## Bankstats and yield-curve registries

Bankstats assets include exact URLs, file types, archive status, member names,
and source hashes. Yield-curve assets distinguish the latest daily bundle from
the archive families and mark that official files may be revised.

```{r asset-registries}
bankstats <- boe_bankstats_assets(limit = 1L)
bankstats[, c(
  "table_label", "url", "file_type", "archive", "member_count",
  "source_page_url", "source_sha256"
)]

yields <- boe_yield_assets()
with(yields, table(scope, frequency))
```

The registries are discovery and identity controls, not copies of the remote
workbooks. A reader checks that the requested URL is an exact registered URL
before downloading it. If a workbook or ZIP changes shape, bounded parsing
fails with a typed condition instead of silently guessing headers or dropping
cells.

## Saved Inflation Report and Monetary Policy Report forecasts

`boe_mpr_releases()`, `boe_mpr_assets()`, `boe_mpr_catalogue()` and
`read_boe_mpr_forecasts()` use an authenticated saved numeric snapshot without
network access or PDF tools. It preserves official forecast vintages,
scenarios, annual/quarterly meanings, missing and censored tokens, source
coordinates and revision receipts across the published archive. Explicit
`boe_mpr_maintain()` checks new reports and historical revisions using official
release dates; it stages source bodies temporarily and discards them by default.
Ordinary reads never run maintenance. Forecast report Resources and any
third-party inputs retain their applicable source notices; the Database OGL
must not be assumed to apply.

## Release families and an explicit missing-snapshot state

`boe_release_registry()` is the affirmative list of audited release families.
`boe_release_assets()` is intentionally separate: it is only available when a
matching pinned asset snapshot has been packaged. The following check reports
the current build's state without making a request. In a build where that
snapshot is absent, the expected result is a `readboe_config` condition; this
is an honest limitation rather than an inferred asset list.

```{r release-registry}
release_families <- boe_release_registry()
release_families[, c("family", "label", "parser")]

release_assets_status <- tryCatch(
  {
    assets <- boe_release_assets(limit = 1L)
    sprintf("available (%d row shown)", nrow(assets))
  },
  readboe_config = function(e) paste("unavailable in this build:", conditionMessage(e)),
  error = function(e) paste("unexpected error:", conditionMessage(e))
)
release_assets_status
```

Do not use a release landing page as if it were an asset receipt. When the
asset snapshot is available, pass an exact URL from `boe_release_assets()` to
`read_boe_release_asset()` and retain the returned provenance.

## Cache and exact provenance

Successful remote responses are cached as success entries only. The default
cache is under `tools::R_user_dir("readboe", "cache")`; a workflow can pass an
explicit directory, such as a project-managed or temporary directory. The
cache contains raw bytes plus identity, response metadata, timestamps, and a
SHA-256 digest. It is not a general-purpose download directory.

This example exercises the offline cache contract in a temporary directory.
`cache_only = TRUE` never falls back to a network request, so an empty cache
produces a typed `readboe_cache_miss` condition.

```{r cache-miss}
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboe-data-sources-cache")
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
removed <- boe_cache_clear(cache_dir)

asset_url <- boe_yield_assets()$url[[1L]]
cache_miss <- tryCatch(
  boe_download_asset(
    asset_url,
    cache_only = TRUE,
    cache_dir = cache_dir
  ),
  readboe_cache_miss = identity
)

c(
  removed_entries = removed,
  condition = class(cache_miss)[[1L]],
  message = conditionMessage(cache_miss),
  cache_files = length(list.files(cache_dir, pattern = "[.]rds$"))
)
```

With network access, the successful path is:

```{r provenance-live, eval=FALSE}
raw <- boe_download_asset(
  asset_url,
  deadline = boe_deadline(seconds = 30),
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
receipt <- boe_provenance(raw)
receipt[c(
  "source_identity", "canonical_url", "final_url", "retrieved_at",
  "raw_bytes", "raw_sha256", "etag", "last_modified", "from_cache",
  "transforms", "package", "package_version"
)]
```

`boe_provenance()` returns `NULL` for an object that is not a successful
`readboe` result with a provenance attribute. Do not manufacture a receipt for
hand-built data: preserve the package's receipt with the result you actually
used, and record any downstream transformations separately.

## Rights and attribution

The package surfaces the official notices that should accompany downstream
data. They are intentionally links and instructions, not a claim that the
package can grant reuse rights.

```{r rights}
boe_rights()
```

Review the Bank's current legal terms, IADB help and data semantics, and the
yield-curve methodology/disclaimer before redistributing observations or
derived products. Preserve official identifiers, footnotes, provisional and
confidentiality markers, revision fields, and source links where relevant.
